newsitem.title: CANADA: BASEBALL-EXPOS BOUNCE MARLINS, AID WILD-CARD CHANCES..
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-EXPOS BOUNCE MARLINS, AID WILD-CARD CHANCES..

text.p: The Montreal Expos gave their wild-card hopes a boost on Thursday, bouncing the Florida Marlins 6-2 and moving a full game ahead of the Los Angeles Dodgers in the chase for a post-season berth.
Mark Grudzielanek drove in two runs and David Segui's run-scoring single off Patt Rapp (6-15) snapped a tie in the sixth inning as the Expos won their sixth straight game.
Rapp allowed four runs, nine hits and five walks over 5 2/3 innings and became the league's first 15-game loser.
Yorkis Perez replaced Rapp in the inning, but walked Andy Stankiewicz to force home a run for a 4-2 advantage.
Barry Manuel (4-1) allowed one hit and struck out one in two scoreless innings for the win.

"These people really wanted to win the ballgame tonight," said Montreal manager Felipe Alou about his team. "They showed a lot of intensity. Everyone got to pick up the slack. There's no pressure, we're supposed to be a last-place team."
In the eighth, Mike Lansing scored on the back end of a double steal. Grudzielanek's run-scoring single plated Rondell White with Montreal's final run in the ninth.
Gregg Colbrunn hit his 15th homer and Santangelo extended his hitting streak to 13 games for Florida.

In Philadelphia, Curt Schilling pitched his fifth complete game of the season and Benito Santiago belted a two-run homer to highlight a three-run first as the last-place Phillies downed the Chicago Cubs 6-1.
Schilling (7-8) allowed six hits while walking one and striking out seven. His only mistake was allowing Brian McRae's 13th homer in the third inning.

The Phillies touched Frank Castill0 (7-15) for three runs in the first. Ricky Otero led off with a triple and Mickey Morandini was hit by a pitch. Gregg Jefferies hit into a fielder's choice, scoring Otero before Santiago's homer.
Gene Schall and Kevin Stocker each had RBI singles in the fourth to extend the lead to 5-1.
Schilling contributed to his own cause by singling in Schall in the fourth, completing the scoring.

"It's always nice to go out with the lead in the second inning and have the other team press to try to do something instead of giving them a run early and let them sit back," said Schilling, who threw 119 pitches.
Castillo (7-15) was tagged for six runs -- five earned -- and seven hits in 3 1/3 innings in the loss.
